# Decision: TBD stable ID and title

Template under the [architecture contract](../../agent-governance/architecture.md).
Create a separate record for a significant decision; routine choices may be stated
briefly in the architecture. Preserve superseded decisions and link replacements.

| Record control | Project value |
| --- | --- |
| Decision ID, owner and author | `TBD` |
| Status | Proposed; record any later decision, authority and date explicitly |
| Decision authority and applicable approval rule | `TBD` project rule; no new approval mandate is implied |
| Scope / architecture reference | `TBD` |
| Requirement, scenario and constraint IDs with source revisions | `TBD` |
| Record revision / reviewed snapshot | `TBD` |

## Problem and drivers

State the actual decision to make, affected stakeholders, relevant constraints and
success criteria. Identify unresolved assumptions and whether they prevent a
binding decision. Link source requirements instead of rewriting their authority.

## Credible options and evaluation

| Option | How it addresses the drivers | Costs, disadvantages and risks | Evidence / uncertainty |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TBD` | `TBD` | `TBD` | Planned or actual, clearly identified |

Consider retaining the current design when meaningful. No fixed alternative count
is required. If only one feasible option remains, explain the actual constraints
that eliminate others. Aesthetic preference alone is not a defect or rationale.

## Proposed choice and consequences

Record the choice, why it fits the prioritized drivers, and which tradeoffs are
accepted or still awaiting authority. Name affected elements, interfaces, data,
operations and implementation plans. Include negative consequences, migration or
reversal cost, compatibility implications and follow-up actions with owners.

## Confirmation and implementation

| Claim / source criterion | Planned check and environment | Owner | Result, inspected revision and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TBD` | `TBD` | `TBD` | Not run |

Decision acceptance, implementation status and observed verification are separate
claims. A review may assess the rationale without proving runtime behavior. Link
actual code/contract changes and deviations when they exist; never infer them from
the decision status. Failed or missing mandatory confirmation remains visible.

## Reconsideration and history

State when changed requirements, invalid assumptions, measured outcomes or cost
would reopen the decision. Record affected trace links, reassessment owner and
superseding record when applicable. History should explain what changed and why;
do not silently rewrite the evidence supporting an earlier decision.
